notes:
Account summary: Closed-lost to direct OpenAI API. Late-stage procurement but technical/legal comfort with direct provider and simpler integration won out.

Recent timeline: 
- 2025-09-02: Inbound lead from webinar; initial qualification (Maya).
- 2025-09-18: Discovery call (SE Liam joined) — primary use: customer support assistant + legal document search for compliance teams. Latency targets ~ <150ms p95 for short chat flows; embedding throughput heavy for nightly batch reindex. Cost sensitivity: medium — priority on predictable unit economics.
- 2025-10-07: Demo of Redwood hosted + dedicated capacity. Showed routing/fallback and KV caching benefits.
- 2025-10-21: Security questionnaire sent; customer flagged data residency and SOC2 evidence. Provided drive:/security/ivorytide-security-answers-2025-11-25.docx.
- 2025-11-19: Technical deep-dive (fireflies ff_2025-11-19_ivorytide_demo). Team expressed desire for minimal ops overhead; primary engineer quoted: "We want something we can ship in weeks, not months."
- 2025-11-26: Procurement panel. CFO raised concerns about premium committed spend for Dedicated; suggested trial of direct provider first due to predictable per-call pricing.
- 2025-12-03: Internal org change — Product Director (champion) accepted new role outside company. Champion drop reduced momentum.
- 2025-12-10: Final call — customer decided to go with OpenAI direct API for initial rollout; plan to revisit multicloud/inference platform once usage matures.

Loss reason (observations):
- Primary reason: simplicity and brand trust of direct OpenAI/Anthropic APIs — lower perceived integration risk and faster TTM.
- Secondary: procurement preference to avoid committed reserved capacity (Dedicated) under uncertain Q1 budget; CFO wanted zero-commit variable costs.
- Tertiary: internal champion left; no executive sponsor to push enterprise procurement/SSO/KMS discussions.
- Security: Redwood answered SOC2/SAML/KMS questions but the team accepted OpenAI's published compliance artifacts and a lighter SSO integration timeline.

What we tried: custom pricing discussion, short-term pilot without long-term commit, technical migration plan showing easy fallbacks, revised security package and staged rollout (hosted -> dedicated). None overcame the simplicity argument.

Next steps (internal):
- Mark as closed-lost; add to quarterly win/loss review (GT M).
- Save demo artifacts and security Q&A to playbook for future similar accounts.
- Reach out in 90 days to check on usage and potential need for cost optimization / Private deployment once regulatory needs firm up.

CRM snippets / rep notes: 
- "They liked the routing and caching ideas but prioritized 'what's fastest to integrate'" — SE Liam.
- "CFO: we can't justify reserved spend for proof-of-concept" — Maya.
- "Follow up Q1 if they hit token cost ceiling or require data residency."
